hindi: उन पानकों के कटु और अम्ल (द्रव्यों) के साथ संयोगों को, तथा द्रव्य और मान को अलग-अलग जानकर (उनके) गुण-कर्म बताने चाहिए।
english: Having known separately the combinations with pungent and sour (substances) of those drinks (pānaka), and the substance and the measure, one should declare (their) qualities and actions.
notes: teṣāṃ pānakānāṃ refers to the drinks named in the preceding verse (279). pṛthak pṛthak 'separately' is taken with vijñāya.

words.gloss: having pungent, sour, sweet and salty (tastes)

hindi: कटु, अम्ल, मधुर और लवण (रस वाले) राग और षाडव लघु, मुख को प्रिय, हृद्य, दीपन और भोजन में रुचि उत्पन्न करने वाले हैं।
english: Rāgas and ṣāḍavas, having pungent, sour, sweet and salty (tastes), are light, pleasing to the mouth, cordial (hṛdya), stimulating digestion and giving relish for food.
notes: rāga and ṣāḍava are kept Sanskrit (names of relish preparations). svādu here is the taste name, sweet.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

words.gloss: because of unctuousness, sweetness and heaviness

hindi: आम्र और आमलक के लेह बृंहण और बल बढ़ाने वाले हैं, तथा स्नेह, मधुरता और गुरुता के कारण रुचिकारक और तर्पण कहे गए हैं।
english: Lehas (linctuses) of āmra and āmalaka are nourishing and increase strength, and they are declared appetizing (rocana) and replenishing (tarpaṇa) because of unctuousness, sweetness and heaviness.

text_flags.why: possible: the first quarter has 7 syllables (ā-mrā-mla-ka-le-hā-śca), one short of 8; āmalaka adds one light syllable and gives 8 (ā-mrā-ma-la-ka-le-hā-śca) with the normal odd-quarter cadence ka-le-hā (⏑ – –) at syllables 5-7

notes: The split follows the suggested reading āmra-āmalaka; the printed āmrāmlaka could also be read āmra-amlaka ('mango and amlaka'), which leaves the quarter a syllable short. āmra = mango (common name).

hindi: संयोग और संस्कार को, तथा उन पर आश्रित द्रव्यों के मान को जानकर, उसी प्रकार उन-उन लेहों के गुण-कर्म बताने चाहिए।
english: Having understood the combination and processing, and the measure of the substances dependent on that, one should likewise state the qualities and actions of each of those lehas.
notes: tacchritam = tat + śritam 'resting on that', i.e. on the combination and processing.

words.gloss: causing moistness (utkleda) of blood, Pitta and Kapha
tubers, roots, fruits and the like

words.gram: n. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ā-√su

hindi: शुक्त रक्त, पित्त और कफ का उत्क्लेद करने वाला और वात का अनुलोमन करने वाला है; और उसमें आसुत कन्द, मूल, फल आदि को वैसा ही जानना चाहिए।
english: Śukta causes moistness (utkleda) of blood, Pitta and Kapha and moves Vāta downward; and one should know tubers, roots, fruits and the like steeped in it to be likewise.
notes: rakta-pitta may also be read as the disease name raktapitta ('causing utkleda of raktapitta and Kapha'); blood and Pitta are given. śukta kept Sanskrit (a sour fermented preparation).

hindi: शिण्डाकी और अन्य आसुत जो काल से अम्ल हो गया हो, रुचिकारक और लघु है। वैद्य (इसे) कृतान्नों का ग्यारहवाँ वर्ग जाने।
english: Śiṇḍākī and other steeped (preparations) (āsuta) soured by time are appetizing and light. The physician should know (this as) the eleventh group, that of prepared foods (kṛtānna).
notes: śiṇḍākī kept Sanskrit. The neuter predicates (kālāmlaṃ rocanaṃ laghu) agree with āsutam anyat and are taken for both. The verse closes the group of prepared foods.

hindi: (तेल) कषाय अनुरस वाला, मधुर, सूक्ष्म, उष्ण और व्यवायी है; पित्तकारक, मल-मूत्र को बाँधने वाला और श्लेष्मा को न बढ़ाने वाला है;
english: (Oil) is sweet with astringent as its subsidiary taste (anurasa), subtle, hot and pervading (vyavāyin); it increases Pitta, binds faeces and urine, and does not increase Kapha (śleṣman);
notes: SENTENCE: the subject tailam is in 287b. No group heading is printed at the start of the food adjuncts here. baddhaviṇmūtra: bahuvrīhi 'by which faeces and urine are bound'.

hindi: वातनाशकों में उत्तम, बल देने वाला, मेधा और अग्नि को बढ़ाने वाला है; संयोग और संस्कार से तेल सब रोगों को दूर करने वाला माना गया है।
english: it is the best among Vāta-destroying (things), strengthening, and increases intellect and the digestive fire (agni); through combination and processing, oil is held to remove all diseases.
notes: SENTENCE: completes 286. GAP: line a has 14 syllables (vā-ta-ghne-ṣū-tta-maṃ-ba-lyaṃ | me-dhā-gni-va-rdha-nam); its second quarter has only 6, so two syllables seem to be missing; nothing is supplied. The oil plant is not named in 286-287.

hindi: तेल के प्रयोग से पूर्वकाल में दैत्यों के अधिपति अजर, विकाररहित, श्रम को जीतने वाले और युद्ध में अत्यन्त बलवान थे।
english: Through the use of oil, the lords of the Daityas were formerly free from ageing, free from disorders, conquerors of fatigue (śrama), and exceedingly strong in battle.
notes: Daitya kept as a name.

words.gloss: removing vātāsṛk, gulma, heart disease and chronic fever
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: ऐरण्ड तेल मधुर, गुरु और श्लेष्मा को बढ़ाने वाला है; वातासृक्, गुल्म, हृद्रोग और जीर्णज्वर को हरने में श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Airaṇḍa oil is sweet, heavy and increases Kapha (śleṣman); it is supreme in removing vātāsṛk, gulma, heart disease and chronic fever (jīrṇajvara).

text_flags.why: the stem asṛk/asṛj ends in a consonant, so asṛk + gulma gives asṛggulma with no vowel a; the printed -ga- gives the half-line 17 syllables (vā-tā-sṛ-ga-gu-lma-…-pa-ram), the correction 16

notes: airaṇḍa is the vṛddhi (derived) form of eraṇḍa, 'of the eraṇḍa'; eraṇḍa = castor (common name). vātāsṛk (vāta + blood) kept Sanskrit. jīrṇajvara literally 'old fever'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva
n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: सार्षप तेल कटु और उष्ण, रक्त और पित्त को दूषित करने वाला, कफ, शुक्र और अनिल को हरने वाला तथा कण्डू और कोठ का नाशक है।
english: Sārṣapa oil is pungent and hot, vitiates blood and Pitta, removes Kapha, semen and Vāta (anila), and destroys itching and koṭha (rash).
notes: sarṣapa = mustard (common name). rakta-pitta may also be the disease name raktapitta. śukra-hara 'removing semen' is rendered literally.

hindi: प्रियाल का तेल मधुर, गुरु और श्लेष्मा को बढ़ाने वाला है; अत्यधिक उष्ण न होने से उसे वात और पित्त के संयोग में हितकर मानते हैं।
english: Priyāla oil is sweet, heavy and increases Kapha (śleṣman); because it is not excessively hot, they hold it beneficial in the combination of Vāta and Pitta.
notes: na atyauṣṇyāt 'from not being excessively hot'. priyāla kept Sanskrit.

hindi: आतस्य (तेल) मधुर और अम्ल है, किन्तु विपाक में कटु; उष्णवीर्य, वात में हितकर और रक्त-पित्त को प्रकुपित करने वाला है।
english: Ātasya (oil) is sweet and sour, but pungent in vipāka (post-digestive effect); it has hot vīrya (potency), is beneficial in Vāta and aggravates blood and Pitta.
notes: ātasya 'of atasī'; atasī = linseed (common name). tu 'but' contrasts the taste with the vipāka.

hindi: कुसुम्भ का तेल उष्ण, विपाक में कटु और गुरु है, और विशेष रूप से विदाही तथा सब दोषों को प्रकुपित करने वाला है।
english: Kusumbha oil is hot, pungent in vipāka and heavy, and especially causes burning (vidāhin); it aggravates all the doṣas.

text_flags.why: 'ciśeṣeṇa' is not a Sanskrit form; viśeṣeṇa 'especially' (व for च) fits the line; same syllable count

notes: kusumbha = safflower (common name).

hindi: फलों के जो अन्य तेल आहार-विधि में प्रयुक्त होते हैं, उन्हें गुण और कर्म में फल के अनुसार बताना चाहिए।
english: The other oils of fruits that are used in the arrangement of food, one should state, as to qualities and actions, according to the fruit.

text_flags.why: possible: printed atha aphalam ('then fruitless') gives no sense with tāni brūyāt and guṇakarmabhyāṃ; yathāphalam 'according to the fruit' takes up phalānāṃ of line a and has the same form as yathāsattvaṃ (295) and yathāsvaṃ (314) in this chunk; same syllable count (dya for da)

notes: The split follows the suggested yathāphalam.

hindi: मज्जा और वैसे ही वसा मधुर, बृंहण, वृष्य और बल देने वाली है; किन्तु वसा और मज्जा की शीतता और उष्णता प्राणी के अनुसार बतानी चाहिए।
english: Marrow (majjan), and likewise muscle-fat (vasā), is sweet, nourishing, aphrodisiac and strengthening; but the coldness and heat of muscle-fat and marrow one should state according to the creature (sattva).
notes: The masculine singular adjectives agree with majjā and are taken for vasā as well. sattva here = the creature (animal) from which the fat or marrow comes.

hindi: विश्वभेषज स्नेहयुक्त, दीपन, वृष्य, उष्ण, वात और कफ को दूर करने वाला, विपाक में मधुर, हृद्य और रुचिकारक है।
english: Dry ginger (viśvabheṣaja) is unctuous, stimulates digestion, is aphrodisiac and hot, removes Vāta and Kapha, is sweet in vipāka, cordial (hṛdya) and appetizing.
notes: viśvabheṣaja = dry ginger, as viśva/nāgara elsewhere in the book (glossary rendering).

hindi: आर्द्र पिप्पली कफकारक, मधुर, गुरु और स्निग्ध है; वह सूखी होने पर कफ और वात का नाश करने वाली, कटु, उष्ण और वृष्य मानी गई है।
english: Fresh pippalī is Kapha-increasing (śleṣmala), sweet, heavy and unctuous; dried, it destroys Kapha and Vāta, is pungent and hot, and is regarded as aphrodisiac.
notes: ārdrā 'fresh, moist' is taken with pippalī against śuṣkā 'dried' in line b. pippalī = long pepper (common name).

hindi: मरिच अत्यधिक उष्ण नहीं, अवृष्य, लघु और रुचिकारक है; छेदी और शोषक होने से वह दीपन और कफ-वात को जीतने वाला है।
english: Marica is not excessively hot; it is not aphrodisiac, is light and appetizing; because it is cutting (chedin) and drying, it stimulates digestion and overcomes Kapha and Vāta.
notes: marica = black pepper (common name).

hindi: हिङ्गु को वात, श्लेष्मा और विबन्ध का नाशक, कटु, उष्ण, दीपन, लघु, शूल को शान्त करने वाला, पाचन और रुचिकारक जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know hiṅgu as destroying Vāta, Kapha (śleṣman) and obstruction (vibandha), pungent and hot, stimulating digestion, light, allaying pain (śūla), digesting (pācana) and appetizing.
notes: hiṅgu = asafoetida (common name). vibandha 'obstruction, binding' (of faeces or wind) is kept with the Sanskrit word.

hindi: सैन्धव, जो लवणों में उत्तम है, रुचिकारक, दीपन, वृष्य, नेत्रों के लिए हितकर, अविदाही, त्रिदोषनाशक और मधुरता से युक्त है।
english: Saindhava, the best of salts, is appetizing, stimulates digestion, is aphrodisiac, good for the eyes and not causing burning, destroys the three doṣas, and has a sweet (taste) with it.

text_flags.why: 'triḍoṣa' with retroflex ḍ is not a Sanskrit form; doṣa is printed with dental d in this chunk (sarvadoṣaprakopaṇam, 293); same syllables

notes: samadhura = sa-madhura 'accompanied by sweetness' (as in 304).

hindi: सूक्ष्मता, उष्णता, लघुता और सुगन्ध के कारण सौवर्चल रुचि देने वाला, विबन्ध का नाशक, हृद्य और उद्गार को शुद्ध करने वाला है।
english: Because of its subtlety, heat, lightness and fragrance, sauvarcala gives relish; it destroys obstruction (vibandha), is cordial (hṛdya) and purifies eructation (udgāra).
notes: sauvarcala kept Sanskrit (a salt).

hindi: तीक्ष्णता, उष्णता और व्यवायी होने के कारण बिड दीपन, शूलनाशक और ऊपर तथा नीचे वायुओं का आनुलोम्य करने वाला है।
english: Because of its sharpness, heat and pervasiveness (vyavāyitva), biḍa stimulates digestion, destroys pain (śūla), and brings the winds (vāta) into their proper direction (ānulomya), upward and downward.
notes: vātānām (plural) is taken as the winds in the body; ānulomya 'going with the grain, proper direction'. biḍa kept Sanskrit (a salt).

hindi: औद्भिद तिक्त और कटु (रसों) से युक्त, क्षार से युक्त, तीक्ष्ण और उत्क्लेद करने वाला है। कालालवण में गन्ध नहीं होती, और (उसके) वे गुण सौवर्चल के गुण हैं।
english: Audbhida (salt) has bitter and pungent (tastes), has alkali (kṣāra) in it, is sharp and causes moistness (utkleda). In kālalavaṇa there is no smell, and its qualities (te) are those of sauvarcala.
notes: te sauvarcalaguṇāḥ: te is read as the qualities of kālalavaṇa; it may also be a bahuvrīhi 'they have the qualities of sauvarcala', referring to the salts. kālalavaṇa literally 'black salt', kept Sanskrit.

hindi: सामुद्रक मधुरता से युक्त है; पांशुज तिक्तता से युक्त और कटु है। सब लवण रुचिकारक, पाकी, स्रंसी और अनिल को दूर करने वाले हैं।
english: Sea salt (sāmudraka) has a sweet (taste) with it; pāṃśuja has a bitter (taste) with it and is pungent. All salt is appetizing, causes digestion (pākin), is laxative (sraṃsin) and removes Vāta (anila).
notes: The comma printed after samadhuraṃ is kept in src and left out of the word. pāṃśuja literally 'born of dust/earth', kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: heart (disease), pāṇḍu, grahaṇī disease, spleen (disorder), ānāha and galagraha

hindi: यावशूक हृदय (रोग), पाण्डु, ग्रहणी रोग, प्लीहा (रोग), आनाह, गलग्रह, कफज कास और अर्श को दूर करता है।
english: Yāvaśūka removes heart (disease), pāṇḍu, grahaṇī disease, (disorder of) the spleen, ānāha (distension), galagraha, cough born of Kapha, and arśas.
notes: roga in the compound may apply to grahaṇī only or to the preceding members too; hṛd and plīhan are rendered with 'disease/disorder' understood. yāvaśūka is a derived word (from yava-śūka 'barley awn'), not split; 306 speaks of every kṣāra (alkali). Disease names kept Sanskrit.

hindi: सब क्षार तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, लघु, रूक्ष, क्लेद करने वाला, पचाने वाला, विदारक, दाहक, दीपन, छेदक और अग्नि के समान है।
english: Every alkali (kṣāra) is sharp and hot, light and dry, causes moistness (kledin), digests (paktṛ), tears (vidāraṇa), burns, stimulates digestion, cuts, and is like fire.

words.gloss: destroying Vāta, Kapha and foul smell
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: कारवी, कुञ्चिका, अजाजी, यवानी, धान्य और तुम्बुरु रुचिकारक, दीपन तथा वात, कफ और दुर्गन्ध का नाश करने वाले हैं।
english: Kāravī, kuñcikā, ajājī, yavānī, dhānya and tumburu are appetizing, stimulate digestion, and destroy Vāta, Kapha and foul smell.
notes: dhānyatumburu is printed as one word without any sandhi change and is split as two names, dhānya and tumburu. The predicates are neuter singular, said of the list as a whole. dhānya here = coriander (common name); the other names are kept Sanskrit.

hindi: आहारयोगियों के विभाग का निश्चय तो नहीं है। और आहारयोगियों का यह बारहवाँ वर्ग पूर्ण हुआ।
english: But for the food adjuncts (āhārayogin) there is no fixed determination of division (bhakti). And this twelfth group, of the food adjuncts, is completed.
notes: bhakti 'division, share': the line says the food adjuncts have no fixed classification or list. The verse closes the twelfth group.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ati-√i

hindi: एक वर्ष से अधिक पुराना शूलधान्य और शमीधान्य प्रशस्त माना जाता है; पुराना प्रायः रूक्ष और नया प्रायः गुरु होता है।
english: Spiked grain (śūladhānya) and pod grain (śamīdhānya) more than a year old are praised; old (grain) is mostly dry, new (grain) mostly heavy.
notes: śūla 'spike' is kept as printed and read as the spiked (awned) ear of grain; śūka 'awn' is a possible reading, but this is a lexical doubt only, so no flag. samātīta = samā 'year' + atīta 'gone past'.

hindi: जो-जो (अन्न) शीघ्र आता है, वह-वह अधिक लघु माना गया है। भूसी रहित और युक्ति से भुना हुआ सूप्य लघु रूप में पचता है।
english: Whatever (grain) comes up quickly is regarded as the lighter. Pulse (sūpya) that is husked and roasted with rational planning (yukti) is digested lightly.

text_flags.why: 'vipacayate' is not a regular form (the passive of vi-√pac is vipacyate); the even quarter then has 9 syllables (sū-pyaṃ-la-ghu-vi-pa-ca-ya-te); vipacyate gives 8 with the even-quarter cadence vi-pa-cya (⏑ – ⏑, pa heavy before cy) at syllables 5-7

notes: āgacchati 'comes (up)' is taken as coming to maturity; the subject is understood from 309 (grain).

hindi: मरे हुए, कृश, अत्यधिक मेद वाले, वृद्ध, अल्पवयस्क, विष से मारे गए, अपने चरने के क्षेत्र से बाहर पाले गए और व्याल द्वारा मारे गए (प्राणी) का मांस त्याग देना चाहिए।
english: One should discard meat (of an animal) that is dead, lean, excessively fat, old, young, killed by poisons, reared outside its pasture (agocara), or killed by a vyāla (vicious animal).
notes: The adjectives are neuter and grammatically qualify māṃsam; the animal is understood. vyāla kept Sanskrit (a vicious beast or snake).

hindi: इससे भिन्न मांस हितकर, बृंहण और बल बढ़ाने वाला है। मांसरस सब प्राणियों को प्रीणन करने वाला और परम हृद्य है।
english: Meat other than this is wholesome, nourishing and increases strength. Meat-juice is gladdening to all beings and supremely cordial (hṛdya).
notes: param 'supremely' may qualify both prīṇanaḥ and hṛdyaḥ.

words.gloss: of those seeking strength and complexion

hindi: सूखते हुए, रोग से मुक्त हुए, कृश, क्षीण रेतस् वाले और बल तथा वर्ण चाहने वालों के लिए भी रस को अमृत के समान जानना चाहिए।
english: For those who are wasting, those freed from disease, the lean, those of depleted semen, and also those who seek strength and complexion, one should know meat-juice (rasa) to be like amṛta (nectar).
notes: rasa here is the meat-juice of 312.

words.gloss: of age, intellect, senses and life-span

hindi: यथायोग्य दिए गए रस को सब रोगों का शमन करने वाला, स्वर के लिए हितकर और वय, बुद्धि, इन्द्रियों तथा आयु को बल देने वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know meat-juice (rasa), prescribed as proper to each (case), as alleviating all diseases, good for the voice, and giving strength to age (vayas), intellect, the senses and the life-span.
notes: yathāsvam 'each according to its own' is taken as 'as proper to each case'. The genitive vayobuddhīndriyāyuṣām is taken with balakaram.

hindi: जो मनुष्य नित्य व्यायाम करने वाले, नित्य स्त्री-सेवी और नित्य मद्य-सेवी हैं, और नित्य मांसरस का आहार करने वाले हैं, वे न आतुर होंगे, न दुर्बल।
english: Men who are constantly given to exercise, to women and to madya, and who always have meat-juice as food, would be neither ill nor weak.
notes: nityaṃ māṃsarasāhārāḥ is read as a further description of the same men; it may also be read as a condition ('if they always eat meat-juice'). madya kept Sanskrit (wine).

words.gloss: damaged by worms, wind or sun
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: कृमि, वायु या धूप से नष्ट, सूखा, पुराना, बिना ऋतु का और बिना स्नेह के पकाया गया शाक, और जो अपरिस्रुत हो, वह वर्जनीय है।
english: A pot-herb (śāka) damaged by worms (krimi), wind or sun, dried, old, out of season, or cooked without fat, and one that is not drained (aparisruta), is to be avoided.
notes: aparisruta 'not drained, from which (the juice) has not been let flow'.

words.gloss: by worms, vyālas, frost or sun
grown in the wrong place and season

hindi: जो फल पुराना, कच्चा, कृमि, व्याल, हिम या धूप से क्षतिग्रस्त, अनुचित देश और काल में उत्पन्न और गीला हो, वह अच्छा नहीं है।
english: Fruit that is old, unripe, damaged by worms (krimi), vyālas, frost (hima) or sun, grown in the wrong place and season, or sodden (klinna) — that is not good.
notes: vyāla kept Sanskrit (as in 311). klinna 'wet, sodden'.

words.gloss: of madya, water, milk products (gorasa) and the rest

hindi: हरितों का निर्देश, साधन को छोड़कर, शाकों के समान है; मद्य, जल, गोरस आदि का निश्चय अपने-अपने वर्ग में है।
english: For greens (harita) the instruction is as for pot-herbs (śāka), except for preparation (sādhana); for madya, water, milk products (gorasa) and the rest, the determination is in their own respective groups.
notes: sādhana 'preparation (cooking)': greens are judged as pot-herbs except in the way they are prepared.

words.gloss: to the qualities of the food

hindi: जो पेय आहार के गुणों से विपरीत हो और जो धातुओं का विरोधी न देखा गया हो, वह अन्न का अनुपान माना जाता है।
english: A drink which is opposite in qualities to the food, and which is seen not to be incompatible with the dhātus, is desired as the after-drink (anupāna) of food.
notes: Read as yat … pānaṃ viparītaṃ … yac ca dhātūnāṃ na virodhi, tad annānupānam iṣyate; annānupānam is taken as the predicate of tad iṣyate.
